newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds strengthen, outperform on dlr rally.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds strengthen, outperform on dlr rally.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Friday, sharply outperforming their U.S. counterparts, amid a rally in the currency and increased expectations of a Bank of Canada rate cut, dealers said.

"The market's already priced it (a rate cut) in," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn. "(The central bank) wants stability in our currency. They don't want it running up the way it's running up."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.85 to C$112.20 to yield 6.983 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 14/32 to yield 6.68 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 31 basis points from 40 points at the close on Thursday.
"It looks like the bank will have room (to cut) again," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities. "Canada continues to enjoy this virtuous circle."

Canadian fixed income market rallied this morning, with T-bills pricing in a rate cut, after the U.S. October employment report came in line with forecasts, increasing expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will not raise rates for the rest of the year.
The belief that the Fed will not raise rates helped the Canadian dollar rally to its strongest point in more than a year. The unit reached the key C$1.3333 (US$0.7500) level in mid-afternoon trade.

The stronger currency has led many to believe that the Bank of Canada will soon cut interest rates for the 11th time this year. In making its three most recent rate cuts, the Bank of Canada cited its desire to offset the tightening impact of a stronger Canadian dollar on monetary conditions. A stronger dollar tightens monetary conditions by making exports less competitive.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.66 to C$104.93 to yield 6.329 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 8/32 to yield 6.37 percent.
The difference in yields went from a positive spread of seven basis points at Thursday's close to a negative spread of four basis points.
The three-month cash bill traded at 2.99 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.16 percent.
